messages.text: Bring me news from the mark first. A map is not a story until someone walks it.
You found {target_article}? Good. A village that can be reached can also be warned.
{target_article}, then. I will mark the road in softer ink. People live at the end of that line.
So {target_article} still stands. Old stone keeps old trouble, but now the way there is honest.
{target_article}. Hm. I will note the hazards twice and the treasure not at all.
You reached {target_article} and came back speaking. That is worth a darker border.
{target_article}, confirmed. Some roofs are warnings. I will draw that one like it bites.
{target_article} under open water. Good work. The sea hides landmarks better than any fog.
You found {target_article}? Then the waves were telling the truth for once.
{target_article}. Timber below ground means somebody trusted the dark too much.
You found {target_article}. I will mark the descent and leave room for cave-ins.
{target_article}. Keep your voice low even in the telling. Some places listen after you leave.
You came back from {target_article}. I will mark it, but not invite anyone there lightly.
{target_article}, found at last. That is not a road; it is a question carved into stone.
You found {target_article}. Some maps point outward. That one points beneath everything.
{target_article}. Even the name makes the parchment feel warmer.
You found {target_article} and returned. I will not ask what followed you in memory.
{target_article}. I will mark patrol risk on every road that brushes near it.
You found {target_article}. Good. A tower seen on a map is a tower avoided in time.
{target_article}. Ruins are never as empty as hopeful travelers claim.
You found {target_article}. I will draw it lightly. The past dislikes being pinned down.
{target_article}. A place built to test feet, nerve, and poor judgment.
You found {target_article}. I will mark it as useful, dangerous, and not for the overconfident.
You found {target_article}. Good. The map was a promise; now it is a record.
{target_article}, confirmed. I will clean up the linework and pretend I was certain all along.

openings.text: Mind the map table. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to reading roads and borders, then.

lines.text: Blank edges on a map make people braver than they should be.
Every road looks safer when someone else drew it.
A lost path can become a warning if enough people survive telling it.
Keep your hands off the map table unless you know where they are going.
The edge of a map is not the edge of the world. It is the edge of our nerve.
Roads look straight until you have to walk them tired.
A wrong turn once taught me more than three careful maps.
Map jokes are easy to fold badly.
You could get lost standing still.
Borders are lines people draw so fear has somewhere neat to stand.
A compass helps with north. It says nothing about wisdom.
Blank space on parchment has a way of daring people to be foolish.
I do not mark every path for every traveler. Some maps are earned.
I lost every road for a while. You marked the way back.
I remember your face like a landmark after a long, wrong journey.
The map of that memory is torn, but your name sits near the center.
I remember wandering inside myself. Then a path opened, and you were beside it.
I remember you, yes. Some routes back home still pass through frightening country.
Thunder shook the map table so hard loose maps tried to fly, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked maps, compasses, and road marks after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the map table, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the maps twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have maps to set right.
I checked dry parchment and map frames for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the map table after.
The maps can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the map table, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the map table, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, maps can wait flat on the table; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the map table still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before maps, compasses, and road marks. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the map table and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the map table, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the map table first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the road past the last torch and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the map table enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a fresh mark on the map between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the map table, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning sand out of the compass case.
I checked maps, compasses, and road marks, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the map table, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a cartographer which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the map table, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
Maps can wait flat on the table. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the map table found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the map table. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing snow off the road signs and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the map table. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.

pacify.text: Fine. I will mark this as settled, lightly, in pencil.
Your count is off. The route to peace is {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
No. Every path back to trust is closed for now.
